counterfactual_missing_items: No hypopigmented macules, periungual fibromas, or Shagreen plaques were present
No family history of TSC or renal disease is provided
No seizures or intellectual disability are mentioned
decisive_items: First biopsy of facial papule showed a dome-shaped lesion with several plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels, compatible with an angiofibroma.
Electron micrograph shows a dermal fibroblast with prominent crystalline inclusions within the cytoplasm and some smaller inclusions forming within lysosomes (magnification ×8000).
Medical history includes requiring a right renal transplant at age 14 years.
response.rationale: R2 uniquely integrates angiofibroma histology, EM crystalline inclusions, early renal transplant, and dental findings; R1 lacks angiofibroma/EM and has no pneumothorax or renal tumor history; R5 and R6 are contradicted by absent characteristic skin findings and incompatible systemic features.

rejected.why: No raw support; cystic fibrosis does not explain angiofibromas, renal transplant, or EM crystalline inclusions, and characteristic skin lesions are absent.

Focal dermal hypoplasia would show atrophic linear lesions and fat herniation, not angiofibromas; it is contradicted by absent hypopigmented macules and lacks renal transplant and EM crystalline inclusions.
